dataset: Wang et al. 2024, TNBC spatial transcriptomics + H&E
platform: Spatial Transcriptomics (Stahl 2016, KTH/Spatial Transcriptomics AB; acquired by 10x Genomics 2018). NOT 10x Visium. 1934 spots/array, 100um spot diameter, 150um center-to-center (corrected 2026-08-24; this field read 200um until then - Wang 2024 Methods states 150um and the lattice measures to it, see CLAUDE.md).
encoder_input_decision: use selection.RData - raw integer counts, tissue-filtered spots (1075 spots x 27567 genes after low-expression filtering), median 16492 UMI/spot. rawCountsMatrices TSVs are normalized + batch-corrected despite the name - do not use for Novae.
raw_counts_format: RData matrix, versioned Ensembl gene IDs, coordinate spot indices (ex. '2x6')
raw_counts_dims_example: 1075 spots x 27567 genes (CN1/C1, tissue-selected, low-expression filtered)
naming_warning: rawCountsMatrices/ contains normalized floats, not raw counts. all.RData = full grid raw counts (1931 spots x 30263 genes). selection.RData = tissue-filtered raw counts (1075 spots x 27567 genes). use selection.RData for Novae.

morans_i_summary.caveat: single subarray only - compute median across all 281 for registered report

cross_modal_registration_note: spot-H&E overlay visually confirmed on CN1/C1

Novae.reason: spatial rho PASS, but platform mismatch (100um spots vs subcellular training)

novae.gap_note: batch correction active by design - gap not a valid QC metric for Novae
novae.platform_mismatch: 100um spots vs subcellular training - documented, not blocking

uni2_reinhard.reinhard_target_selection: closest to grand mean LAB across alignment training set
uni2_reinhard.rho_note: slight decrease across all subarrays - Reinhard removes spatially-correlated stain variation entangled with biological signal
uni2_reinhard.interpretation: modest effect on single-institution data. dominant variation is biological, not staining protocol. real test is alignment Recall@K

pca_hvg.gap_note: dominated by patient/batch identity - first PCs separate subarrays, not biological structure
pca_hvg.rho_sign_note: positive rho (nearby spots more similar) vs negative for UNI2/Novae - PCA-HVG captures gene expression gradients directly

design_implications.alignment_asymmetry: UNI2 ~50 effective dims vs Novae ~11. ST projection head does more work expanding sparse signal into 512-d shared space

mlp_options.novae_bottleneck: LayerNorm(64) -> Linear(64, 16) -> GELU -> Linear(16, 512) -> GELU -> Linear(512, 512)

design_implications.reinhard_tension: biological and technical signal partially entangled in same PCs - cannot perfectly separate

risks: Novae GNN tissue compatibility uncertain on TNBC original-ST (100um spots) - validate embedding UMAP in phase 1
Moran's I computed on single subarray (CN1/C1) - compute median across all 281 for registered report
MKI67 spatial autocorrelation lower than expected (I=0.19) - check consistency across subarrays
17 subarrays with <500 selection spots - monitor for downstream impact
resolved_risks: encoder_input_decision resolved 2026-04-01: raw integer counts found in selection.RData (byArray/{slide}/{subarray}/). rawCountsMatrices name is misleading - contains normalized floats.

batch_effect_analysis.asymmetry_note: UNI2 encodes patient identity (56x chance), Novae does not. ComBat on UNI2 only is the correct targeted intervention.

alignment_findings.alignment_unit_decision: spot level insufficient for cross-patient at 100-200um resolution with 200 cells/spot
alignment_findings.next_unit: region/archetype - Wang et al. 14 megacluster labels available on Zenodo
alignment_findings.mc_labels_source: Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.8135721, per-spot MC assignments for all 281 subarrays
alignment_findings.karpathy_loop_status: tier 2 complete, pivot to alignment unit change (requires new exp series)

normalization_finding.virchow2: ImageNet mean/std only via timm create_transform, no stain normalization
normalization_finding.uni2_reinhard: Reinhard applied BEFORE timm transform - may be suboptimal
normalization_finding.uni2_reinhard_combat_all: Reinhard + ComBat - same concern, used in failed exp02
normalization_finding.source: community practice: Virchow2/UNI2 trained on diverse multi-institution data, learned stain invariance during pretraining
normalization_finding.implication: stain normalization removes variation the model was trained to handle, can hurt performance
normalization_finding.action: Virchow2 extraction uses timm transform only (correct). UNI2 reinhard work may need reanalysis if morphology classification underperforms
normalization_finding.supporting_evidence: PathoROB Komen et al. 2025 - Virchow2 robustness index 0.88, highest of 20 FMs evaluated

morphology.denominator: tissue pixels only (background excluded from fraction calc)
morphology.imbalance_note: immune class is 5x rarer than stroma - use stratified sampling and per-class F1 for rank 1a

tls_scores.source: 30-gene TLS signature (Cabrita et al. 2020 panel) on raw counts from selection.RData
tls_scores.normalization: log1p of count-normalized expression, mean across panel genes

mc_labels_hard.source: clustering/intraPatientClust + Kmeans MC/km14.RDS - Wang et al. megacluster scheme
mc_labels_hard.method: intra-patient k-means (k=2..10 selected per patient), then global k-means (k=14) on cluster prototypes
mc_labels_hard.imbalance_note: MC7 0.6% is 24x rarer than MC4 14.6% - need stratified sampling and per-class F1

mc_weights_soft.method: non-negative matrix factorization, each spot is mixture of 14 megacluster gene programs
mc_weights_soft.interpretation: per-spot continuous cell-state composition (rich biological signal at sub-spot resolution)

purity_stats.interpretation: 61.5% of spots have one dominant program, 96.6% have a clear dominant

mc_weights_soft.use_case: rich ST representation for alignment (replaces or complements novae 64-d)

encoder_qc_comparison_2026-04-09.method: patient-stratified linear probe + cross-subarray silhouette + within-subarray silhouette + batch effect ratio against MC labels (14-class) and morphology labels (5-class)

uni2_raw_pilot_only.note: only pilot subarrays extracted at scale, never run on full 280. UNI2_reinhard was extracted but uses banned preprocessing.

encoder_qc_comparison_2026-04-09.decision: Virchow2 niche is primary H&E encoder - 23.6% MC linear probe (3.3x chance) vs Novae 12.1% (1.7x), morph 57.1% vs 33.0%, only encoder with positive cross-subarray morphology silhouette

virchow2_normalization_decision.test: z-score per subarray (same as Novae test)
virchow2_normalization_decision.verdict: z-score HURTS Virchow2 - cuts linear probe MC accuracy in half (23.6% -> 10.4%)
virchow2_normalization_decision.interpretation: Virchow2's per-subarray mean is biologically meaningful, not technical artifact. removing it destroys real signal. opposite of Novae behavior.
virchow2_normalization_decision.scientific_finding: Novae z-score helps (+0.11 silhouette), Virchow2 z-score hurts (-13.2% probe). different encoders need empirically validated preprocessing decisions, not assumed.
virchow2_normalization_decision.supports_pathoROB: Virchow2 robustness index 0.88 (highest of 20 FMs in PathoROB benchmark) is empirically reproduced here - Virchow2 already encodes cross-subarray morphological structure in raw embedding space
virchow2_normalization_decision.decision: Use Virchow2 niche RAW - no z-score, no normalization beyond timm create_transform

cca_diagnostic_2026-04-09.purpose: understand what CCA is capturing in baseline before launching alignment training
cca_diagnostic_2026-04-09.test_setup: 20 subarrays subset, per-component CCA + held-out subarray test

q1_which_st_component_drives_cca.method: fit CCA per subarray with different ST input combinations, average R@1
q1_which_st_component_drives_cca.finding: mc_weights drive almost all CCA signal. adding novae HURTS (rich ST 79d worse than mc_w 14d alone). novae acts as noise CCA cannot filter.

q2_within_vs_cross_subarray.method: fit CCA on 19 train subarrays, evaluate on 1 held-out
q2_within_vs_cross_subarray.finding: CCA's high within-subarray R@1 is COMPLETELY patient-leakage shortcut. cross-subarray collapses to literal zero. all baselines (random ~0.001, late fusion ~0.0025) are essentially random for cross-subarray retrieval.

implications_for_rank2: the genuine alignment problem is cross-subarray and is unsolved
any cross-subarray R@1 > 0.01 from the MLP is a meaningful novel result
novae adds noise to CCA but may still be useful as within-subarray spatial context

circular_dependency_caught_2026-04-09.issue: rank2 v1 design used mc_weights in both ST input AND positive pair definition
circular_dependency_caught_2026-04-09.consequence: model would learn to predict its own input, not H&E -> biology mapping
circular_dependency_caught_2026-04-09.fix: separate biological supervision from ST features

rank2_v2_design.st_input: novae(64) + pathway_embed(d) + cytotrace(1) + tls(1) - NO mc_weights
rank2_v2_design.supervision: soft InfoNCE targets from mc_weight cosine similarity
rank2_v2_design.principle: mc_weights teach the model what biological similarity means without being features it can cheat on

rank1a.split: 5-fold patient-stratified CV (74-78 train patients, 16-21 test patients per fold)
rank1a.interpretation: linear probe on hard labels underestimates alignment potential - InfoNCE uses soft mc_weights (continuous 14-d) which contain richer signal than argmax labels. MC7/MC8 failure reflects morphological ambiguity of rare programs at linear probe level, not absence of signal.
rank1a.next: rank2 - InfoNCE alignment Virchow2 niche (1280) vs rich ST (79-d), per-subarray batches, mc_weight cosine positive pairs

h_e_encoder.preprocessing: timm create_transform only (ImageNet mean/std), no z-score, no Reinhard, no ComBat
h_e_encoder.extraction_method: k=6 spatial neighbors mean pool of CLS tokens

committed_alignment_plan.positive_pair_definition: (Virchow2 patch[i], rich_ST[j]) where same subarray AND cosine(mc_weights[i], mc_weights[j]) > 0.8
committed_alignment_plan.hard_negative_definition: (Virchow2 patch[i], rich_ST[k]) where same subarray AND cosine(mc_weights[i], mc_weights[k]) < 0.3
committed_alignment_plan.training_design: per-subarray batches with biology-driven positive pairs
committed_alignment_plan.evaluation: test BOTH within-subarray AND cross-subarray retrieval against CCA, late fusion, unaligned baselines. report both.
committed_alignment_plan.validation_gate: rank1a (linear probe Virchow2 niche -> MC 14-class, patient-stratified 5-fold CV) must achieve macro-F1 > 0.3 before running alignment training

filtered_graph_test.test: removed background-dominated spots before Novae graph construction, re-ran inference
filtered_graph_test.interpretation: graph quality (artifact spots in neighborhood) is NOT the issue. filtering does not improve geometry.

z_score_test.method: z-score Novae embeddings within each subarray independently
z_score_test.interpretation: half of cross-subarray problem (0.111 of 0.246) was per-subarray mean shift, half is genuine geometric inconsistency across cohort. linear probe accuracy unchanged - signal magnitude is platform-limited not normalization-limited.

novae_decision.within_subarray_status: weak positive structure - real local biological signal
novae_decision.decision_rationale: Novae works locally per-subarray but does not produce cross-subarray comparable embeddings. The proposal allows within-subarray evaluation which sidesteps this entirely.

mc_weights.role: primary biological signal, cross-patient stable by construction

novae.role: within-subarray spatial context, NOT used for cross-subarray comparison

novae_decision.positive_pair_definition: (Virchow2 patch[i], rich_ST[j]) where same subarray AND cosine(mc_weights[i], mc_weights[j]) > 0.8 - biology-driven not just spatial co-registration
novae_decision.hard_negative_definition: (Virchow2 patch[i], rich_ST[k]) where same subarray AND cosine(mc_weights[i], mc_weights[k]) < 0.3 - forces model to distinguish cell programs not just locations
novae_decision.evaluation_scope: within-subarray retrieval (R@K, MRR) against CCA/late-fusion/unaligned baselines, per-subarray ARI vs SAs/MCs for H2, per-subarray CCA for H3
novae_decision.scope_note: this decision is specific to TNBC-92 (Wang et al. 100um spot platform). Novae trained on Xenium subcellular ST - cross-platform mismatch. other datasets may not need within-subarray restriction.

key_finds.clustering/MC deconv/: per-spot 14-MC soft NMF weights (270k spots) - cell-state level signal
key_finds.clustering/clustPrototypes/: per-MC gene expression prototypes (for pathway projection)
key_finds.deconvolution/: per-patient cell-type expression prototypes (8 categories: Tumor/Stroma/Lymphocyte/Vessels/etc) - per-patient only, NOT per-spot
key_finds.classification/projectedSamples/: per-patient PCA projection [n_spots x 500] + spot identifiers in subarray.spot_id format

zenodo_data_extended_2026-04-09.no_cell_level_st: no Xenium/MERFISH/CosMx/CODEX in this dataset. cell-state signal comes via NMF soft decomposition (mc_weights), not subcellular ST.

pc_concept_lock.observation: top-5 mc-locked PCs == top-5 patient-locked PCs. mc signal and patient architecture share the same linear subspace.

patient_ablation_niche.procedure: fit PCA(50) on niche, rank by eta2_patient, project out top-k, recompute batch_ratio + lp_mc
patient_ablation_niche.outcome: entangled - batch_ratio only drops below cell at k=20, at which point lp_mc has collapsed from 3.1x to 1.5x chance. no knee. linear residualization cannot separate signals.

virchow2_cell_vs_niche_interp_2026-04-10.biological_interpretation: RECONCILED FRAMING: 'niche encodes patient identity' and 'niche encodes MC program' are the same statement, not two. in TNBC, a patient's TME architecture IS their MC program mixture. PC1 captures e.g. 'immune-rich MC3+MC7 patient' vs 'tumor-dominant MC4+MC11 patient' - that single direction is simultaneously patient ID and MC identity because in this biology they are defined by each other. the entanglement is biological fact, not noise contamination to remove. linear residualization fails because there is nothing separate to project out.
virchow2_cell_vs_niche_interp_2026-04-10.rank2_decision: linear residualization dead. three options: (1) cell encoder - lp_mc 0.190, br 0.585, honest, lower ceiling, patient less dominant; (2) niche + domain-adversarial GRL - nonlinear separation of within-vs-between patient variation, paper-worthy; (3) niche + within-subarray eval only - limited scope, patient shortcut persists. defaulting to (2). paper motivation is 'prevent InfoNCE patient shortcut', NOT 'remove batch effect'. cell encoder is honest fallback baseline.
virchow2_cell_vs_niche_interp_2026-04-10.paper_hook: PC1 carries 17% variance simultaneously encoding both MC and patient identity - regime where domain-adversarial methods are designed to operate.
do_not_redo: do not re-run linear residualization hoping for a different k - curve is monotone entangled
do not use niche cross-subarray retrieval as rank 2 eval without adversarial debiasing
whitespace/stain probing is not the bottleneck - do not pursue before adversarial experiment
virchow2_cell_vs_niche_interp_2026-04-10.real_problem: the problem is NOT patient signal contamination. the problem is that within-subarray InfoNCE uses patient identity as a shortcut: two spots from the same patient share TME architecture, so the model matches them by patient without learning cross-modal morphology->program alignment. this is why CCA within-sub R@1=0.667 collapsed to 0.000 cross-subarray.
virchow2_cell_vs_niche_interp_2026-04-10.what_adversarial_does: NOT 'remove patient signal to expose MC signal' (they are the same signal). YES 'force the shared space to encode what differentiates spots within a patient's TME, not between patients'. within-patient variation is where genuine cross-modal signal lives. GRL finds the nonlinear subspace orthogonal to the dominant patient-architecture axis.
